Article 7

1. The community has obligations and responsibilities in providing Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence.
2. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against Women and Children to the competent authorities;
c. providing emergency assistance; and
d. providing protection to victims of violence.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Bangli Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Bangli Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangli.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangli Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a Woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for the Child or those who have power over the Child.
10. Violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence.
12. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly.
13. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of Violence from the Regional territory to the Region of origin.
14. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
15. Legal Aid is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, assisting, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
17. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regency government to provide services to Women and Children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid.
18. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children victims of violence.
19. Pakraman Village is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unity of tradition and etiquette of social life of Hindu communities passed down through generations within the bond of Kahyangan Tiga or Kahyangan Desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household;
20. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to:

a. prevent all forms of violence against Women and Children;
b. protect Women and Children and provide services to Women and Children Victims of Violence; and
c. empowerment of Children Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER VIII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 13

1. The Regional Government conducts monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children victims of violence.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children victims of violence in the Region.

Article 14

1. Monitoring is conducted through coordination and direct monitoring of relevant Regional Apparatus on a regular basis.
2. Monitoring is conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children victims of violence for the current year.

CHAPTER VII

SOCIAL PROTECTION HOUSES

Article 12

1. The Regional Government is obligated to establish Social Protection Houses and/or Safe Houses.
2. Social Protection Houses and/or Safe Houses as referred to in paragraph (1) shall guarantee the implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, and social reintegration services.
3. In the event that victims experience trauma or illness that endangers themselves as a result of acts of violence requiring immediate assistance, the Regional Government is obligated to provide first aid no later than 7 (seven) days after the complaint is filed.
4. For the provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government may utilize social protection houses and/or Safe Houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 17

1. The Regent conducts guidance on the development of PPT.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. provision of implementation instructions;
b. counseling;
c. supervision; and
d. monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of services for Women and Children victims of violence, both apparatus and community.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of Women and Children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of Women and Children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for Women and Children.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against Women and Children in Bangli Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children victims of violence in Bangli Regency.

Article 15

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or if necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XIII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 21

In the event that the PPT as referred to in Article 8 paragraph (1) has not been established, the existing P2TP2A shall continue to carry out the duties and functions of integrated services for Women and Children victims of violence in the Region.

CHAPTER XII

FUNDING

Article 20

Funding for the provision of protection to Women and Children Victims of violence shall be sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

REGENT OF BANGLI

PROVINCE OF BALI

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANGLI REGENCY

NUMBER 18 OF 2016 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

CHAPTER IX

REPORTING

Article 16

1. The Regent is responsible for preparing a report on the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence and submitting it to the Governor with a copy submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.
2. Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.
3. The form of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 18

The Regent conducts guidance and supervision over the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Regency area.

2. Regional Government is the Government of Bangli Regency.

5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a Woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for the Child or those who have power over the Child.
10. Violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence.
12. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly.
13. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of Violence from the Regional territory to the Region of origin.
14. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
15. Legal Aid is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, assisting, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.

18. 20. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to:

a. prevent all forms of violence against Women and Children;
b. protect Women and Children and provide services to Women and Children Victims of Violence; and
c. empowerment of Children Victims of Violence.

Article 7

1. The community has obligations and responsibilities in providing Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence.
2. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against Women and Children to the competent authorities;
c. providing emergency assistance; and
d. providing protection to victims of violence.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of Women and Children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of Women and Children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for Women and Children.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against Women and Children in Bangli Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children victims of violence in Bangli Regency.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of Women and Children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of Women and Children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for Women and Children.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against Women and Children in Bangli Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children victims of violence in Bangli Regency.

I. GENERAL

In order to prevent and overcome violence against Women and Children in Bangli Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children victims of violence in Bangli Regency.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against Women and Children in Bangli Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children victims of violence in Bangli Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Bangli Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Bangli Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangli.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangli Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a Woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for the Child or those who have power over the Child.
10. Violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence.
12. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly.
13. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of Violence from the Regional territory to the Region of origin.
14. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
15. Legal Aid is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, assisting, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
17. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regency government to provide services to Women and Children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid.
18. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children victims of violence.
19. Pakraman Village is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unity of tradition and etiquette of social life of Hindu communities passed down through generations within the bond of Kahyangan Tiga or Kahyangan Desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household;
20. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of Women and Children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of Women and Children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for Women and Children.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against Women and Children in Bangli Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children victims of violence in Bangli Regency.

c. supervision; and
d. monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of services for Women and Children victims of violence, both apparatus and community.

Article 7

1. The community has obligations and responsibilities in providing Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence.
2. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against Women and Children to the competent authorities;
c. providing emergency assistance; and
d. providing protection to victims of violence.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of Women and Children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of Women and Children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for Women and Children.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against Women and Children in Bangli Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children victims of violence in Bangli Regency.

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to:

a. prevent all forms of violence against Women and Children;

c. empowerment of Children Victims of Violence.

Article 7

1. The community has obligations and responsibilities in providing Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence.

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 13

Article 15

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or if necessary according to needs.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of Women and Children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against Women and Children in Bangli Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children victims of violence in Bangli Regency.

1. Monitoring is conducted through coordination and direct monitoring of relevant Regional Apparatus on a regular basis.

FUNDING

Article 20

Funding for the provision of protection to Women and Children Victims of violence shall be sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

SOCIAL PROTECTION HOUSES

Article 12

1. The Regional Government is obligated to establish Social Protection Houses and/or Safe Houses.

4. For the provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government may utilize social protection houses and/or Safe Houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

As is known, the human rights of Women and Children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of Women and Children from violence should be respected, upheld and enhanced in human dignity without discrimination, welfare and justice for Women and Children.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against Women and Children in Bangli Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children victims of violence in Bangli Regency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Bangli Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Bangli Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangli.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangli Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a Woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for the Child or those who have power over the Child.
10. Violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence.
12. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly.
13. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of Violence from the Regional territory to the Region of origin.
14. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
15. Legal Aid is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, assisting, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
17. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regency government to provide services to Women and Children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid.
18. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children victims of violence.
19. Pakraman Village is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unity of tradition and etiquette of social life of Hindu communities passed down through generations within the bond of Kahyangan Tiga or Kahyangan Desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household;
20. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
